designs.title: Summit Ridge
designs.why: Strong diagonal: the ridge climbs from lower left to the far summit at top right, and the five roped climbers sit right where the eye lands, crisp at full size. No type is needed. The weak spot is the pale band between the far range and the near ridge, where the mid-ground breaks into loose dashes and specks. From 3 m that makes the design read as two separate blocks, not one deep scene.
designs.fix: Close the middle gap with a few more connecting slopes, or move the near ridge up about 300 px, and clean up the stray specks. The far range and the climbers' ridge should read as one continuous mass.

designs.title: Beluga
designs.why: The S-curve of the body is elegant and the letterspaced serif caption is tasteful. But the outline is so thin and the stipple so sparse that the whale is mostly empty shape. Along the edges the stipple breaks into dash fragments that look like noise, not tone. The caption sits small, off to the right under the tail, so it doesn't hold the page's axis, and a large dead area is left at lower right.
designs.fix: Thicken the outline and pack the stipple into a deliberate tonal gradient along the belly and flank. Then center the caption on the page axis at about 1.3x its current size so it anchors the composition.

designs.title: Patagonia
designs.why: The best composition of the four. The centered Fitz Roy spire makes a clear apex, the ranges recede well into a single vertical panel, and the PATAGONIA plus coordinates lockup is well spaced and well matched. The labels let it down. At about 2.5 mm cap height they are too small to read and risky as white ink on black. San Lorenzo is labeled 3,706 m but drawn far lower than the 3,405 m Fitz Roy, which looks like an error to anyone who reads it.
designs.fix: Enlarge the peak labels to at least 5 mm cap height with heavier leader lines. Either drop San Lorenzo or acknowledge the perspective, so the drawn heights no longer contradict the numbers.

designs.title: Belize
designs.why: The island vignette is lively and well drawn, and the jetty gives a good lead-in. But the typography clashes. BELIZE is set in a heavy geometric sans with a thin rule, while the coordinates are in a light serif, so the two lines don't read as one system. The art is weighted hard to the right, with the hut, jetty and pilings bunched there. The design also stops at about 79% of the canvas height, so it sits high and top-heavy on the back.
designs.fix: Set BELIZE and the coordinates in one family, either both letterspaced serif or both sans, with the rule matched to the heading's width. Rebalance the vignette by bringing the jetty in from the right edge or adding mass at lower left.
